fullPassage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers predict what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by forecasting who you are expected to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who resemble you.

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where (A)[behavioral / superficial] and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce (B)[massive / minimal] volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers (C)[predict / ignore] what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by forecasting who you are expected to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who resemble you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) behavioral=행동의, (B) massive=대규모의, (C) predict=예측하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① behavioral — massive — predict: 원문 일치. 행동(behavioral) 데이터가 기록되고, 대규모(massive) 양의 데이터를 생산하며, 미래 행동을 예측(predict)한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② superficial — massive — predict: (A) superficial(피상적인)은 behavioral(행동의)과 의미가 다름. 데이터의 성격을 나타내는 것이지 깊이를 말하는 것이 아님
❌ ③ behavioral — minimal — predict: (B) minimal(최소한의)은 massive(대규모의)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ behavioral — massive — ignore: (C) ignore(무시하다)는 predict(예측하다)의 반의어 방향으로 부적절
det.tip: behavioral and interactional data(행동 및 상호작용 데이터) / massive volumes(대규모 양) / predicts what you want(예측하다)

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is (A)[recorded / deleted]: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. (B)[increasingly / rarely], this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by (C)[evaluating / fabricating] who you are right now, but by forecasting who you are expected to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who resemble you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) recorded=기록된, (B) increasingly=점점 더, (C) evaluating=평가하는
det.analysis:
❌ ① recorded — rarely — evaluating: (B) rarely(거의 ~않는)는 increasingly(점점 더)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② deleted — increasingly — evaluating: (A) deleted(삭제된)는 recorded(기록된)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ③ recorded — increasingly — evaluating: 원문 일치. 데이터가 기록(recorded)되고, 점점 더(increasingly) 사용되며, 현재의 당신을 평가(evaluating)하는 것이 아니라 예측으로 결정한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ recorded — increasingly — fabricating: (C) fabricating(날조하는)은 evaluating(평가하는)과 의미가 전혀 다름
det.tip: data is recorded(기록되다) / Increasingly, this data is used(점점 더) / not by evaluating(평가하는 것이 아니라)

questions.passage: Think of the (A)[totality / fragment] of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers predict what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by (B)[forecasting / recalling] who you are expected to become, based on patterns (C)[extracted / inserted] from the data trails of millions of others who resemble you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) totality=전체/총체, (B) forecasting=예측하는, (C) extracted=추출된
det.analysis:
❌ ① totality — forecasting — inserted: (C) inserted(삽입된)는 extracted(추출된)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② fragment — forecasting — extracted: (A) fragment(단편)는 totality(전체)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ totality — recalling — extracted: (B) recalling(회상하는)은 forecasting(예측하는)과 의미가 반대 방향(과거 vs 미래)
✅ ④ totality — forecasting — extracted: 원문 일치. 상호작용의 총체(totality)를 생각하고, 누가 될지 예측(forecasting)하며, 패턴이 추출(extracted)된다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: the totality of your interactions(상호작용의 총체) / by forecasting(예측함으로써) / patterns extracted from(~에서 추출된 패턴)

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your ①<u>interactions</u> where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities ②<u>produce</u> massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers ③<u>conceal</u> what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that ④<u>affect</u> your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by forecasting who you are expected to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who resemble you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 스트리밍 서비스가 시청 희망 콘텐츠를 '예측한다'는 맥락. conceal(숨기다)은 predict(예측하다)의 반의어 방향으로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① interactions — 원문 일치. '행동 및 상호작용(interactions) 데이터가 기록되는'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② produce — 원문 일치. '일상 활동이 대규모 데이터를 생산(produce)한다'는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ conceal — 원문은 predict(예측하다). conceal(숨기다)로 바꾸면 '스트리밍 서비스가 시청 희망을 숨긴다'가 되어 데이터 활용 목적과 정반대 ←정답
❌ ④ affect — 원문 일치. '삶에 영향을 미치는(affect) 많은 결정'이라는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch — 스트리밍이 시청 희망을 예측(predict)한다

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These ①<u>occasional</u> activities produce massive ②<u>volumes</u> of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers predict what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how ③<u>risky</u> you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by forecasting who you are expected to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who ④<u>resemble</u> you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 쇼핑, 검색, 소통 등이 '일상적인' 활동이라는 맥락. occasional(간헐적인)은 daily(일상적인)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① occasional — 원문은 daily(일상적인). occasional(간헐적인)로 바꾸면 쇼핑, 검색 등을 '간헐적 활동'이라 하여 대규모 데이터 생산 논리와 모순 ←정답
❌ ② volumes — 원문 일치. 'massive volumes of data(대규모 양의 데이터)'라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ risky — 원문 일치. '보험 회사가 당신이 얼마나 위험한지(risky) 예측'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ resemble — 원문 일치. '당신과 닮은(resemble) 수백만 타인의 데이터'라는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: These daily activities produce massive volumes — 이 일상적(daily) 활동들이 대규모 양을 생산

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to ①<u>describe</u> your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers predict what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will ②<u>perform</u> in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by forecasting who you are ③<u>expected</u> to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who ④<u>oppose</u> you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 당신과 '닮은' 수백만 타인의 데이터 패턴이라는 맥락. oppose(반대하다)는 resemble(닮다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① describe — 원문 일치. '과거 행동을 기술(describe)하는 데 사용'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② perform — 원문 일치. '직업에서 얼마나 잘 수행(perform)할지 예측'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ expected — 원문 일치. '될 것으로 기대되는(expected) 사람'이라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ oppose — 원문은 resemble(닮다). oppose(반대하다)로 바꾸면 '당신에게 반대하는 수백만 타인'이 되어 유사 패턴 추출 논리와 모순 ←정답
det.tip: millions of others who resemble you — 당신과 닮은(resemble) 수백만 타인

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: volumes=양/분량 (일상 활동이 대규모 양의 데이터를 생산한다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① volumes: 원문 일치. 'massive volumes of data(대규모 양의 데이터)'라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② patterns: patterns(패턴)은 massive와 어울리지만 'of data'와 결합 시 데이터 생산 맥락에 부적절
❌ ③ decisions: decisions(결정)은 데이터 생산이 아닌 데이터 활용 결과에 해당
❌ ④ interactions: interactions(상호작용)는 데이터의 양이 아닌 데이터 발생 장면을 나타냄
det.tip: massive volumes of data — 대규모 양(volumes)의 데이터

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: forecasting=예측하는 (현재를 평가하는 것이 아니라 미래를 예측함으로써 결정한다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① evaluating: evaluating(평가하는)은 'not by evaluating'에서 부정되는 대상으로, 빈칸(but by ___)에는 부적절
❌ ② remembering: remembering(기억하는)은 과거 지향적이라 미래 예측 맥락과 맞지 않음
✅ ③ forecasting: 원문 일치. 'not by evaluating... but by forecasting(예측함으로써)'라는 대조 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ questioning: questioning(의문을 제기하는)은 결정을 내리는 방법이 아닌 의문 제기
det.tip: not by evaluating... but by forecasting — 평가하는 것이 아니라 예측(forecasting)함으로써

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: extracted=추출된 (수백만 타인의 데이터 흔적에서 추출된 패턴)
det.analysis:
❌ ① recorded: recorded(기록된)는 데이터 수집 단계이지 패턴 도출 단계가 아님
✅ ② extracted: 원문 일치. 'patterns extracted from the data trails(데이터 흔적에서 추출된 패턴)'이라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ expected: expected(기대된)는 패턴의 처리 방식이 아닌 사람의 상태를 나타냄
❌ ④ predicted: predicted(예측된)는 패턴 자체가 아닌 결과물의 성격을 나타냄
det.tip: patterns extracted from the data trails — 데이터 흔적에서 추출된(extracted) 패턴

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 massive와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: massive=거대한/대규모의 → enormous=거대한/막대한
det.analysis:
❌ ① trivial: trivial(사소한)은 massive(거대한)의 반의어
✅ ② enormous: enormous(거대한/막대한)은 massive(거대한)의 동의어 ←정답
❌ ③ gradual: gradual(점진적인)은 크기가 아닌 속도를 나타냄
❌ ④ selective: selective(선택적인)은 크기가 아닌 선별 여부를 나타냄
det.tip: massive = enormous = 거대한, 대규모의

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 affect와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: affect=영향을 미치다 → influence=영향을 미치다
det.analysis:
✅ ① influence: influence(영향을 미치다)는 affect(영향을 미치다)의 동의어 ←정답
❌ ② prevent: prevent(방지하다)는 영향의 방향과 다름
❌ ③ measure: measure(측정하다)는 영향이 아닌 수치 파악
❌ ④ reflect: reflect(반영하다)는 영향을 미치는 것이 아닌 되비추는 것
det.tip: affect = influence = 영향을 미치다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 increasingly와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: increasingly=점점 더 → progressively=점진적으로/점점 더
det.analysis:
❌ ① slightly: slightly(약간)는 정도가 작음을 나타내어 increasingly와 반대 방향
❌ ② temporarily: temporarily(일시적으로)는 지속 기간이지 증가 정도가 아님
❌ ③ randomly: randomly(무작위로)는 증가 방향이 아닌 무질서를 나타냄
✅ ④ progressively: progressively(점진적으로)는 increasingly(점점 더)의 동의어 ←정답
det.tip: increasingly = progressively = 점점 더, 점차

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 likely와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: likely=~할 가능성이 있는 ↔ unlikely=~할 가능성이 없는
det.analysis:
❌ ① probable: probable(가능성 있는)은 likely의 동의어
❌ ② certain: certain(확실한)은 가능성이 높은 쪽이라 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ frequent: frequent(빈번한)는 가능성이 아닌 빈도를 나타냄
✅ ④ unlikely: unlikely(가능성이 없는)는 likely(가능성이 있는)의 정확한 반의어 ←정답
det.tip: likely(~할 가능성이 있는) ↔ unlikely(~할 가능성이 없는)

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers predict what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by forecasting who you are expected to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who <u>resemble</u> you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 resemble와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: resemble=닮다 ↔ differ from=~와 다르다
det.analysis:
❌ ① imitate: imitate(모방하다)는 resemble(닮다)과 유사한 방향
✅ ② differ from: differ from(~와 다르다)은 resemble(닮다)의 정확한 반의어 ←정답
❌ ③ compare to: compare to(~에 비유하다)는 유사점을 찾는 행위로 반의어가 아님
❌ ④ relate to: relate to(~와 관련되다)는 닮음이 아닌 관련성을 나타내어 반의어가 아님
det.tip: resemble(닮다) ↔ differ from(~와 다르다)

questions.passage:
(A) Your phone <u>predicts</u> what you want to type, suggesting words before you finish.
(B) The ancient oracle <u>predicted</u> that the kingdom would fall within a year.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 predict(s/ed)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) predict=데이터 기반 추정/예측, (B) predicted=신탁에 의한 예언
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 예언하다 — (B) 추측하다: (A)는 데이터 기반이라 '예언'보다 '추정'이 적절, (B)는 신탁이라 '추측'보다 '예언'이 적절
❌ ② (A) 선고하다 — (B) 경고하다: predict에 '선고'나 '경고'의 의미는 없음
✅ ③ (A) 추정하다 — (B) 예언하다: (A)는 알고리즘이 입력 패턴에서 추정하는 것, (B)는 신탁이 초자연적으로 예언하는 것 ←정답
❌ ④ (A) 분석하다 — (B) 보장하다: predict는 분석이나 보장이 아닌 예측
det.tip: (A) 기술적 예측(데이터 기반 추정) vs (B) 신비적 예언(초자연적 예언)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the act of judging or calculating the quality, importance, or value of something"

det.korean: evaluating=평가하다: 어떤 것의 질, 중요성, 가치를 판단하거나 계산하는 행위
det.analysis:
❌ ① forecasting: forecasting(예측하다)은 미래를 추정하는 것이지 가치를 판단하는 것이 아님
❌ ② commuting: commuting(통근하다)은 이동 행위로 판단과 무관
❌ ③ extracting: extracting(추출하다)은 끌어내는 행위이지 판단이 아님
✅ ④ evaluating: evaluating(평가하다)은 질, 중요성, 가치를 판단하는 행위라는 영영 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
det.tip: evaluating = judging the quality, importance, or value of something

questions.passage: Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service __________ (predict) what you want to watch.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: predict → predicts: Your streaming service(3인칭 단수)에 맞춰 동사에 -s를 붙여야 한다
det.analysis: 주어 Your streaming service(3인칭 단수) + 현재 시제 → 동사에 -s 필요: predicts
det.tip: Your streaming service predicts — 3인칭 단수 주어이므로 predict → predicts

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is __________ (record): shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: record → recorded: 수동태(is + 과거분사) 구조에서 과거분사 형태가 필요
det.analysis: data is __________ (record) — 주어 data가 기록'되는' 것이므로 수동태(is recorded). 과거분사 recorded가 필요
det.tip: data is recorded — be동사 + 과거분사 = 수동태. 데이터가 기록된다

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers predict what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating __________, but by forecasting who you are expected to become, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who resemble you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: who you are right now=현재 당신이 누구인지 (현재의 평가가 아닌 미래 예측으로 결정이 이루어진다는 대조 구조)
det.analysis:
❌ ① what you want to watch: 시청 희망 콘텐츠는 스트리밍 서비스의 예측 대상이지 evaluating의 대상이 아님
✅ ② who you are right now: 'not by evaluating ___ but by forecasting who you are expected to become'에서 현재의 당신(who you are right now)과 미래의 당신(who you are expected to become)의 대조 구조에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ how risky you are: 위험도는 보험 회사의 예측 대상이지 evaluating의 대상이 아님
❌ ④ what you are likely to buy: 구매 가능성은 소매업체의 예측 대상이지 evaluating의 대상이 아님
det.tip: not by evaluating who you are right now — 현재 당신을 평가하는 것이 아니라

ch: what you are likely to buy

questions.passage: Think of the totality of your interactions where behavioral and interactional data is recorded: shopping, browsing, communicating, commuting, exercising. These daily activities produce massive volumes of data. Increasingly, this data is used not just to describe your past behavior but to _______________. Your streaming service predicts what you want to watch. Your phone predicts what you want to type. Retailers predict what you are likely to buy. Insurance companies predict how risky you are. And hiring platforms predict how well you will perform in a job. The result is a world in which many decisions that affect your life are made not by evaluating who you are right now, but by forecasting __________, based on patterns extracted from the data trails of millions of others who resemble you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 당신이 될 것으로 기대되는 사람 (미래 예측 기반 의사결정의 핵심)
det.analysis:
❌ ① how well you will perform in a job: 직무 수행 능력은 채용 플랫폼의 개별 예측 항목이지 forecasting의 궁극적 대상이 아님
❌ ② what you want to type: 입력 희망 내용은 폰의 예측 항목이지 글의 결론부 forecasting 대상과 다름
✅ ③ who you are expected to become: 'by forecasting ___'에서 미래에 될 당신을 예측한다는 맥락에 정확히 부합. 현재(right now)와의 대조 구조 ←정답
❌ ④ how risky you are: 위험도는 보험 회사의 개별 예측 항목이지 전체 결론의 forecasting 대상이 아님
det.tip: forecasting who you are expected to become — 미래에 될 당신을 예측. not A(현재) but B(미래) 대조

ch: how well you will perform in a job
